defaults.permitted_development: In Wales, demolishing a house, part of a house or an outbuilding is not automatically free from control. The local planning authority may need to approve the method of demolition and site restoration through a prior approval process before work starts, and separate listed building or conservation area consent can still be required.

rules.height_rules: There is no demolition height right. The key question is whether the proposal falls within the demolition procedures and whether the building has heritage status.
rules.depth_rules: There is no depth allowance. Partial demolition or associated rebuilding works are judged on their own facts.
rules.boundary_rules: Temporary hoarding, access changes, scaffolding, highway occupation and disposal of rubble are separate regulatory issues. Demolition that destabilises adjoining land or boundary structures can trigger extra approvals.
rules.roof_rules: Stripping roof coverings or taking down a roof as part of demolition should not be treated as an isolated permitted step if the overall project needs prior approval or heritage consent.
rules.materials_rules: Site restoration and waste handling matter. Salvage, recycling and safe removal of asbestos or contaminated material are separate legal duties.

The local planning authority may need to approve the method of demolition and site restoration through a prior approval process before work starts, and in tighter urban areas the sequence of works, site safety and treatment of adjoining structures can be critical.

rules.height_rules: There is no demolition height allowance. The key issue is whether the proposal falls within the demolition procedures and whether any heritage consent is needed.
rules.depth_rules: There is no depth allowance. Partial demolition, facade retention and the relationship to adjoining buildings are planning and building-control issues in their own right.
rules.boundary_rules: Temporary hoardings, scaffold over sail, highway occupation, rubble removal and support to neighbouring walls are separate regulatory matters. Urban demolition is rarely just a simple knock-down exercise.
rules.roof_rules: Stripping roof coverings or taking down a roof should not be treated as an isolated permitted step if the overall project needs prior approval, heritage consent or structural coordination with adjoining property.
rules.materials_rules: Site restoration and waste handling matter. Salvage, asbestos, contaminated materials and recycling duties sit alongside the planning route.

restrictions.conservation_area: Demolition in a conservation area can need conservation area consent and early discussion with the local planning authority.
restrictions.listed_building: Demolition of a listed building, or of curtilage structures that form part of its special interest, needs listed building consent.

rules.permitted_development: In Wales's national parks, demolition is not something to assume away as minor work. The local planning authority may need prior approval for the method of demolition and site restoration, and heritage or landscape issues often make early discussion essential.

rules.height_rules: There is no demolition height right. The main issues are whether prior approval is required and whether the building or its setting has heritage value.
rules.depth_rules: There is no depth allowance. Partial demolition, retaining plinths or exposed slabs, and the extent of ground reinstatement can all matter in a sensitive landscape.
rules.boundary_rules: Temporary hoarding, access changes, scaffolding, highway occupation and disposal of rubble are separate regulatory issues. Demolition that destabilises adjoining land or boundary structures can trigger extra approvals. In a national park, heritage value and the effect of loss on the wider setting are usually examined very carefully.
rules.roof_rules: Taking down the roof is part of the overall demolition project and should be considered with the whole heritage and restoration package.
rules.materials_rules: The authority may focus closely on how the site will be restored and whether useful traditional materials are to be salvaged rather than simply discarded.
